IBU101.title: Unsafe URL blocked
IBU101.why: A link, image, form or frame received a URL with a dangerous scheme such as javascript:, vbscript: or data:text/html. Clicking or loading it would run attacker code (XSS). Browsers ignore tabs, newlines and control characters inside URLs, so IbuJS parses URLs exactly like the browser before checking them.
IBU101.fix: Only http(s), mailto, tel, sms and relative URLs are allowed (plus blob: and image/audio/video data: URLs for media src). If the URL comes from users, validate it when you save it: s.string({ url: true }). The blocked attribute is replaced with about:blank#blocked; the page keeps working.
IBU101.example: Website // safe: a javascript: value is neutralised

IBU102.title: Raw HTML or inline event handler blocked
IBU102.why: innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, srcdoc, outerHTML, http-equiv and string event handlers (onclick="...") turn text into running code or markup. They are the most common source of XSS, so IbuJS has no way to use them.
IBU102.fix: Render children instead of HTML strings, and pass functions as handlers. For user-written rich text, use a Markdown renderer that outputs IbuJS elements, or render it on a separate sandboxed origin.

IBU103.title: Element cannot be rendered
IBU103.why: <script> elements created from components execute, and <base> silently changes how every relative URL on the page resolves. Both are classic injection targets.
IBU103.fix: Load scripts from index.html or import them as modules. Set <base> in index.html if you really need it.
IBU103.example: import confetti from './confetti.js'   // instead of rendering <script src=...>

IBU104.title: Invalid element or attribute name
IBU104.why: Element and attribute names must be plain identifiers. Names built from data could otherwise smuggle markup.
IBU104.fix: Use literal tag names in JSX. If you spread objects into props ({...data}), pick the fields you need instead.

IBU105.title: A function was used as a child
IBU105.why: Functions cannot be shown on screen. This usually means a missing call or a component written as {MyComponent}.
IBU105.fix: Call it ({renderList()}) or render it as a component (<RenderList />).

IBU106.title: An object was used as a child
IBU106.why: Plain objects (for example a whole API response) cannot be rendered. IbuJS also refuses them because JSON shaped like an element could otherwise inject markup.
IBU106.fix: Render the field you want, or stringify it for debugging.

IBU107.title: Invalid style value
IBU107.why: style must be an object of CSS properties or a CSS string.
IBU107.fix: Use an object with camelCase names; numbers get px automatically where that makes sense.

IBU108.title: Unsafe <style> content during server rendering
IBU108.why: Text inside <style> is not escaped by browsers. A "</" sequence could close the style tag and start real HTML.
IBU108.fix: Never put user input inside <style>. Use the style prop for dynamic values.

IBU109.title: SafeHtml cannot be created directly
IBU109.why: SafeHtml marks HTML that IbuJS produced and escaped itself. Letting code wrap arbitrary strings would bring back XSS.
IBU109.fix: Build HTML with the html`` template, renderPage() or renderToString(); all three escape their inputs.

IBU201.title: Mount target not found
IBU201.why: createApp() could not find the element to render into.
IBU201.fix:
Add
to index.html and load your script with type="module" so it runs after the page is parsed.

IBU203.title: Infinite update loop
IBU203.why: Something writes to a signal that it also reads, so every update triggers another one.
IBU203.fix: Do not change signals while rendering. Move writes into event handlers or effects, and read with signal.peek() when you need the value without subscribing.
IBU203.example: effect(() => { total.value = items.value.length })   // fine: reads items, writes total

IBU204.title: Duplicate keys in a list
IBU204.why: Keys tell IbuJS which item is which when a list changes. Duplicates make it reuse the wrong DOM nodes (inputs keep the wrong text, animations jump).
IBU204.fix: Use a unique, stable id per item, not the array index.

IBU205.title: bind needs a writable signal
IBU205.why: bind keeps an input and a signal in sync in both directions, so it needs the signal object itself.
IBU205.fix: Pass the signal, not its value.

IBU301.title: Router refused to leave the site
IBU301.why: router.navigate() only moves between pages of your own app. Accepting other origins would let a crafted ?next= parameter send users to a phishing site.
IBU301.fix: Use a normal <a href="https://..."> for external links.

IBU302.title: router.navigate() needs a browser
IBU302.why: There is no address bar on the server.
IBU302.fix: On the server, render the route you need directly or send a redirect with ctx.redirect().

IBU303.title: api() needs a browser
IBU303.why: api() calls your own server from the page. On the server there is no page origin to call.
IBU303.fix: On the server, call your functions or database directly instead of over HTTP.
IBU303.example: const notes = await db.sql`SELECT * FROM notes`

IBU304.title: api() only calls your own server
IBU304.why: Sending requests (with cookies) to other origins from the page leaks data and API keys. api() resolves the URL like fetch would, so tricks such as //evil.com or /\evil.com are caught.
IBU304.fix: Call third-party APIs from your server, where keys stay secret, and expose your own route.

IBU401.title: Request body too large
IBU401.why: The upload exceeded maxBodyBytes (1 MB by default). Unbounded bodies let anyone exhaust server memory.
IBU401.fix: Raise the limit only where needed: createServer({ maxBodyBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024 }).

IBU402.title: Expected JSON
IBU402.why: ctx.body() reads JSON and requires Content-Type: application/json. This also prevents simple cross-site form posts.
IBU402.fix: Send JSON from the page with api.post(path, data), which sets the header for you.

IBU403.title: Body is not valid JSON
IBU403.why: The request body could not be parsed.
IBU403.fix: Send JSON.stringify(data) or use api.post(), which does it for you.

IBU404.title: Not found
IBU404.why: No route or file matches this path and method.
IBU404.fix: Check the path and HTTP method, and that the route is registered before app.listen().

IBU405.title: Invalid route definition
IBU405.why: Routes must start with "/", have a handler, and be defined once.
IBU405.fix: app.get('/path', ctx => ctx.json({ ... })). Remove duplicate definitions.

IBU406.title: Unsafe CORS configuration
IBU406.why: Allowing every origin ("*") together with cookies would let any website act as your logged-in users.
IBU406.fix: List the exact origins that may call your API with credentials.

IBU407.title: ctx.html() needs escaped HTML
IBU407.why: A plain string could contain injected markup. html``, renderPage() and renderToString() escape user data automatically.
IBU407.fix: Wrap your markup with one of those helpers.

IBU408.title: Redirect to another site refused
IBU408.why: Redirecting to a URL taken from the request (?next=...) lets attackers bounce your users to phishing pages that look like they came from you.
IBU408.fix: Redirect to paths on your own site. For trusted external targets, check them against an allowlist and pass { allowExternal: true }.

IBU409.title: Method not allowed
IBU409.why: The path exists but not for this HTTP method. The Allow header lists the methods it supports.
IBU409.fix: Use the right method (GET reads, POST creates, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE removes) or add a route for it.

IBU410.title: Route finished without a response
IBU410.why: The handler returned without calling ctx.json(), ctx.text(), ctx.html(), ctx.redirect() or ctx.empty(). Usually a missing await or return.
IBU410.fix: Make sure every path through the handler sends a response, and await async work first.
IBU410.example: app.get('/api/notes', async ctx => { ctx.json(await db.sql`SELECT * FROM notes`) })

IBU411.title: next() called twice
IBU411.why: A middleware called next() more than once, which would run the rest of the chain twice.

IBU412.title: Cross-site request blocked (CSRF protection)
IBU412.why: A browser tried to send a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to your server from another website. Without this check, any site could perform actions as your logged-in users.
IBU412.fix: Requests from your own pages, curl and server-to-server calls are allowed automatically. If another site of yours must call this API, add it: createServer({ cors: { origins: ['https://other.example'] } }) or { csrf: { trustedOrigins: [...] } }.

IBU413.title: Bad request target
IBU413.why: The request line did not start with a path (for example an absolute URL meant for a proxy).
IBU413.fix: Nothing to do in your app; clients must request paths like /api/notes.

IBU414.title: Request body could not be read
IBU414.why: The client disconnected or sent a broken upload.

IBU415.title: Validation failed
IBU415.why: The data did not match the schema. The response lists each problem in issues: [{ path, message }].
IBU415.fix: Show the messages next to the matching form fields, or fix the data your page sends.
IBU415.example: const note = await ctx.body(s.object({ text: s.string({ min: 1, max: 200 }) }))

IBU416.title: Too many requests
IBU416.why: The client exceeded the rate limit. Retry-After says how many seconds to wait.
IBU416.fix: Slow down, or raise the limit for this route: rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowMs: 60_000 }). Behind a proxy set createServer({ trustProxy: true }) so users are told apart.

IBU501.title: Weak session secret
IBU501.why: Sessions are signed with this secret; anyone who can guess it can log in as any user.
IBU501.fix: Run `npx ibu secret`, put the value in .env as SESSION_SECRET, and load it with process.env.SESSION_SECRET. Never commit it.

IBU502.title: Password does not meet the policy
IBU502.why: Passwords must be 12+ characters (and at most 1 KB). Length matters more than symbols.
IBU502.fix: Show the message to the user. Encourage passphrases.

IBU503.title: Login required
IBU503.why: The route called sessions.require(ctx) and there is no valid session cookie.
IBU503.fix: Log in first. In the page, catch ApiError with status 401 and show the login form.

IBU504.title: Session needs a user id
IBU504.why: sessions.issue()/login() needs the user's id as a non-empty string.

IBU505.title: Invalid cookie settings
IBU505.why: Browsers reject or weaken cookies with invalid names, SameSite=None without Secure, or __Host- cookies with a domain or non-root path.
IBU505.fix: Use simple names, keep the defaults (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure on HTTPS), and only use SameSite=None over HTTPS.

IBU601.title: Unsafe SQL identifier
IBU601.why: Column and table names cannot be query parameters, so they must be validated separately.
IBU601.fix: Check the name against a list of your columns before calling sql.identifier().

IBU602.title: db.query() needs sql``
IBU602.why: Building SQL by gluing strings together is how SQL injection happens. sql`` sends values separately from the query text, so injection is impossible.
IBU602.fix: Use the tagged template. For hand-written parameterised SQL there is db.raw(text, params), which `ibu check` reviews.
IBU602.example: await db.sql`SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = ${id}`

IBU603.title: SQLite not available
IBU603.why: The built-in node:sqlite module needs Node.js 22.13 or newer.
IBU603.fix: Upgrade Node.js, or use memoryDatabase() while prototyping, or another database through createDatabase(adapter).

IBU701.title: Hard-coded secret
IBU701.why: API keys, passwords and private keys in source code end up in git history, screenshots and AI prompts. Leaked keys are found by bots within minutes.
IBU701.fix: Move it to .env (which is git-ignored) and read process.env.NAME. Rotate the key if it was ever committed or shared.

IBU702.title: Server secret used in browser code
IBU702.why: Everything in the browser bundle is public. Environment variables or AI SDKs used there would expose your keys to every visitor.
IBU702.fix: Keep secrets and @ibujs/ai in src/server.ts and call your own API route from the page.
IBU702.example: for await (const chunk of api.stream('/api/ask', { prompt })) answer.value += chunk

IBU703.title: Raw HTML sink
IBU703.why: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML and document.write turn strings into live markup (XSS).
IBU703.fix: Render JSX children instead. Use textContent if you must touch the DOM directly.

IBU704.title: Dynamic code execution
IBU704.why: eval, new Function and string timers run strings as code; any user data reaching them is remote code execution.
IBU704.fix: Use real functions, JSON.parse for data, and lookup tables instead of building code.

IBU705.title: SQL built from strings
IBU705.why: Interpolating or concatenating values into SQL text allows SQL injection.
IBU705.fix: Use db.sql`... ${value}`, which sends values separately.
IBU705.example: await db.sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ${email}`

IBU706.title: Shell command built from strings
IBU706.why: exec() runs a shell; user data inside the command string can run any command on your server.
IBU706.fix: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and no shell, and validate inputs against an allowlist.

IBU707.title: File path from user input
IBU707.why: Passing request data into file paths can read or overwrite files outside the intended folder (../../.env).
IBU707.fix: Map ids to known files, or validate with s.id() and resolve inside a fixed folder. For public files use serveStatic().

IBU708.title: Request body used without a schema
IBU708.why: Unvalidated input lets clients send wrong types, huge strings or extra fields such as isAdmin: true.
IBU708.fix: Pass a schema: ctx.body(s.object({ ... })). It also gives you TypeScript types.
IBU708.example: const { text } = await ctx.body(s.object({ text: s.string({ min: 1, max: 200 }) }))

IBU709.title: External redirect allowed
IBU709.fix: Only use it with a fixed URL or after checking the target against an allowlist.

IBU710.title: Math.random() on the server
IBU710.why: Math.random() is predictable and must never be used for tokens, ids, codes or passwords.

IBU711.title: Weak hash
IBU711.why: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken and far too fast for passwords.
IBU711.fix: Use hashPassword()/verifyPassword() for passwords and SHA-256 for checksums.

IBU712.title: Security protection disabled
IBU712.why: csrf: false, rejectUnauthorized: false or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED turn off protections against forged requests or intercepted connections.
IBU712.fix: Remove the override; if a specific trusted origin needs access, add it to trustedOrigins instead.

IBU713.title: CORS allows every origin
IBU713.why: Any website can read responses from this API.
IBU713.fix: List the specific origins that need access.

IBU714.title: Signal mutated in place
IBU714.why: notes.value.push(x) changes the array but not the signal's identity, so nothing re-renders.
IBU714.fix: Create a new array or object.

IBU715.title: .env is not git-ignored
IBU715.why: Your secrets would be committed and pushed.
IBU715.fix: Add .env to .gitignore. If it was already committed, rotate every secret in it.

IBU716.title: Session secret written in code
IBU716.why: A literal secret is visible to anyone with the code and is the same in every environment.
IBU716.fix: createSessionManager({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET! }) and generate the value with `npx ibu secret`.

IBU801.title: @ibujs/ai loaded in the browser
IBU801.why: The AI helper needs your API key, which must never reach the browser.
IBU801.fix: Use it only in server code and stream answers to the page through your own route.
IBU801.example: app.post('/api/ask', ai.route({ system: 'You are a helpful cooking assistant.' }))

IBU802.title: No Anthropic API key
IBU802.why: AI features call Claude, which needs an API key.
IBU802.fix: Create a key at https://platform.claude.com, add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... to .env, and restart. Never put the key in code.

IBU803.title: AI is busy
IBU803.why: Too many AI requests are running at once, or the AI provider is rate limiting you.
IBU803.fix: Retry shortly. Raise maxConcurrent or requestsPerMinute in ai.route() if your plan allows.

IBU901.title: Project file missing
IBU901.why: The CLI could not find an entry file listed in ibu.config.json.
IBU901.fix: Check the client/server/html paths in ibu.config.json.

IBU902.title: Nothing built yet
IBU902.why: `ibu start` runs the production build, which does not exist yet.

IBU903.title: AI suggestion rejected
IBU903.why: The AI proposed writing outside your project, into protected files (.env, node_modules, packages), or code that fails the security check.
IBU903.fix: Rephrase the request, or apply the change by hand after reviewing it.
